questions.question: What does `"5" + 3` evaluate to in JavaScript?
questions.explanation: When either operand of + is a string, + joins text, so 3 is converted to "3" and the result is "53".

questions.question: Which statement about const and let is correct?
options: const variables can be reassigned, let variables cannot
let is the older keyword that modern code avoids
A const variable cannot be reassigned to a different value; let can
questions.explanation: const creates a label that can never point at a different value, while let allows reassignment. The older keyword modern code avoids is var.

questions.question: What is the difference between a JavaScript engine and a runtime?
options: There is no difference; the words are synonyms
The runtime executes code; the engine provides APIs like document and fetch
The engine only exists in browsers, the runtime only in Node
The engine executes JavaScript; the runtime is the engine plus environment APIs such as document or file access
questions.explanation: Engines like V8 run the language itself, and a runtime (a browser or Node) wraps the engine and adds environment-specific APIs.

questions.question: Why does `0.1 + 0.2` print 0.30000000000000004?
options: JavaScript numbers are binary floating point, which cannot represent some decimals exactly
It is a bug in Node.js that browsers do not have
Because + converts both numbers to strings first
Because 0.1 is stored as a bigint
questions.explanation: JavaScript numbers are IEEE 754 binary floating point, so values like 0.1 are approximations — which is why money is best stored in whole paise.
